items.title: Nuclear power is back on Southeast Asia's energy agenda
items.description: Rising electricity demand, shocks in energy security and climate commitments are reviving long-stalled plans for nuclear power across Southeast Asia. But proponents of nuclear energy still face formidable obstacles.

items.title: Google hit with €403m fine by Irish data watchdog over GDPR violations
items.description: The penalty follows an inquiry launched into the tech giant six years ago, following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations.

items.title: As US and China talk, middle powers jostle for position
items.description: China's Xi Jinping is traveling to Washington this week. Regardless of what comes from his talks with US President Trump, the EU will likely remain stuck between erratic US trade policy and Beijing's export machine.

sections.title: Beyond Climate & EU — World News Highlights

items.title: UK should 'team up' with Canada in new Europe alliance, Canadian minister tells BBC
items.description: It comes after European Commission President proposed "opening the door" for Canada to become an associate member of the EU.

items.title: Russia: Putin party retains majority in controlled parliamentary vote
items.description: Vladimir Putin's United Russia won just under 58% of the vote, the electoral commission said. Meanwhile, Putin ally Ramzan Kadyrov won nearly 100% of the vote in elections in the Russian republic of Chechnya.
